findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and has confusing, dead logic
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`. It then returns false whether `enabled` is true or false, so the feature flag is never consulted for the result. The name suggests flag-based behavior, but the function is a hard-coded disable. The inverted `enabled` variable and the identical return branches look like a bug and will confuse maintainers. A plain `return false`, or removing the function and returning the error directly, would be clearer. The `h` parameter is also unused in effect.

findings.title: Misleading error message for a deliberately disabled feature
findings.body: A user who has enabled the `sqlExpressions` feature flag gets `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. That wrongly suggests the feature is unfinished rather than disabled for security reasons. The message should say the feature is disabled. The flag is also still documented, so users will be confused.

findings.title: Other entry points to SQL commands are not blocked, only the reader
findings.body: The disable check is added only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (called from the legacy node-building path) still calls `NewSQLCommand` without any gate. It fails only because the stub `TablesList` errors with 'not implemented', and that error is surfaced as a misleading 'error reading SQL command'. Security therefore depends on a stub rather than an explicit check at the command level. The disabled path also returns a generic invalid-SQL error instead of a clear message.

findings.title: Dead code and no tests for the disabled behavior
findings.body: `TablesList` always fails now because the stubbed DB's `RunCommands` returns 'not implemented'. The JSON AST parsing, `tablesFromAST` and the `jeremywohl/flatten` dependency are unreachable except through existing tests. No test was added to verify that the SQL query type is rejected, so a future regression that re-enables execution would go unnoticed. Existing parser and SQL command tests that depended on DuckDB may now fail or need updating.
